fields.name: Titus
fields.description:
Meet Titus, a striking Mustang who joined the ranch back in 2022 as a yearling right alongside Henry, coming all the way from the Stinking Water herd management area in Oregon.

Right from the start, Titus has carried himself with a natural, bold confidence. He proudly displays the heavier bone structure and classic draft horse influence characteristic of the Stinking Water herd. Under saddle, he is an absolute blast to ride—fearless, forward-moving, and never hesitating to blaze his own path when it's time to leave the beaten trail.

fields.name: Tidd Bit
fields.description:
Meet Tidd Bit, affectionately known around the barn as Tid. This charming Haflinger pony has all the raw ingredients to turn into an absolute standout mount.

Tid has previous riding under his belt, but due to changes in his previous rider's circumstances—and with David and me both a bit too big to put in the saddle ourselves—he is currently looking for his next big opportunity.

He can be a little shy when you first approach him, but he has a sweet nature and responds wonderfully to attention. With just a little bit of consistent work and groundwork, Tid is going to make someone a fantastic, dependable little pony.

fields.name: Henry
fields.description:
Meet Henry, a remarkable 5-year-old Mustang hailing from the Palomino Buttes herd management area in Oregon. We welcomed Henry to the ranch as a yearling, and watching him grow into his potential has been an incredible journey—he is now David’s trusted primary riding horse.

Henry embodies everything you could want in a modern equine partner. He is exceptionally smart, possesses a wonderfully smooth gait under saddle, and has an innate desire to please his rider at every turn. Whether out on the trail or working around the property, his willing attitude and steady demeanor make him an absolute standout all-around horse.

fields.name: Dancer
fields.description:
Meet Dancer, one of the cherished senior statesmen of the property. With a pedigree tracing back to a mustang mother and a father that was either a quarter horse or—given his trademark stubborn streak—quite possibly a mule, Dancer has always had plenty of character.

While he used to be an absolute blast to ride under saddle, time and some health considerations have caught up with him. Nowadays, Dancer has officially traded his working days for a life of pure leisure. He spends his time soaking up the sun and hanging out with the rest of the old guys in the pasture, living out his well-deserved retirement in total comfort.

fields.name: Reno
fields.description:
Meet Reno, a character with quite a history around the ranch who is now officially retired and enjoying the pasture alongside Dancer.

Reno is a horse of two halves. While he has playfully (and dramatically!) contributed to a few of David’s broken bones over the years under saddle, he is a completely different story from the ground. On the lead rope and in daily handling, Reno is an absolute gentleman—gentle, kind, and easy to manage.

fields.name: Rook
fields.description:
Meet Rook, the newest addition to our ranch family. A striking bay Mustang, Rook brings a unique blend of curiosity and caution to the barn.

He is a genuinely peculiar horse when it comes to everyday desensitization: things that usually send other green horses running—like fly spray, swinging ropes, and hosing down with water—don't seem to faze him a bit. However, he remains noticeably jumpy and cautious around people.

We are currently taking things slow and focusing heavily on building a solid foundation of mutual trust. Mustangs require patience, and with steady persistence, we have no doubt we will win him over completely.

fields.name: Ty
fields.description:
Meet Ty, who is enjoying a peaceful retirement in the pasture alongside Dancer and Reno.

Ty has always been on the more reserved side, carrying a natural shyness that requires a little extra patience when it's time to catch him. However, once you have him haltered, his demeanor flips entirely. Ty is a willing listener who always tries his best to do whatever is asked of him. While he has been under saddle a few times in the past, he unfortunately never quite made it out to experience the open trails, but he is living out his retirement years in comfort and peace.

fields.name: Doc Ripper
fields.description:
Meet Doc Ripper, affectionately known around the property as Ripp. At just 7 months old, this young Australian Shepherd is already packing an incredible amount of personality, brains, and heart into one fluffy package.

Ripp is easily one of the most loving and affectionate pups you’ll ever meet, and he has made it his full-time job to stick right by his dad, Dwight, every second of every day. True to his breed, he is smart as a whip and picks up on things in a flash. We have high hopes for Ripp as he grows—we have plans for him to be shaped to tackle some serious stock work and turn into the ultimate, reliable trail dog.

fields.name: Pedro
fields.description:
Meet Pedro, the legendary burro who has been around the ranch forever. We are not entirely sure how old he is, other than somewhere around the age of dirt!

Despite his advanced years, age certainly hasn't slowed him down or dulled his sharp personality. Pedro can still happily dish it out when it's time for routine chores like deworming or hoof trimming, keeping everyone on their toes. Over the years, he has successfully contributed to plenty of bruises—both physical and of the ego—for both David and Dwight.

Nowadays, Pedro spends his time hanging out in the pasture with the rest of the old-guy crew, enjoying his well-earned status as the resident boss burro.

fields.title: Tidd Bit - Friendly Haflinger Gelding Looking for His Perfect Partner
fields.description:
Tidd Bit is a handsome, friendly Haflinger with a kind personality and a willing attitude. He was originally purchased for a rider who is unfortunately no longer able to ride. Due to our family's size and riding needs, Tidd Bit has not been getting the saddle time he deserves.

He is a sweet horse who enjoys attention and is easy to be around. Tidd Bit would thrive in a home where he can receive consistent riding and become someone's trusted partner. This is a difficult decision, but we would love to see him with a family or rider who can give him the time and opportunities he deserves.
